frozen_candidate_root_contribution: The root contributes the notion of a BINDING COMMITMENT/UNDERTAKING: a solemnly established obligation that binds a party to a stipulated course of action, thereby creating a standing liability to fulfill it (and a corresponding possibility of breach). It denotes neither the future act promised nor the tightness of ratification, but the bond-of-obligation itself — an engagement laid upon or entered into by parties, which stands open to being kept, honored, cast off, or held accountable.

internal_discovery.plain_explanation:
Across all three form-families the same residue — "a binding obligation/undertaking" — is recoverable once morphology and construction are subtracted.

FORM I (عَهِدَ / أَعْهَدْ, 6 occ.): construed with إِلَى + recipient (+ أَنْ clause), it is a unilateral laying-on of a binding charge. 20:115 "We laid a charge upon (عَهِدْنَا إِلَى) Adam... but he forgot"; 2:125 "We charged (عَهِدْنَا إِلَى) Abraham and Ishmael that: purify My House"; 36:60 "Did I not lay upon you (أَعْهَدْ إِلَيْكُمْ) an engagement that you not worship Satan?"; 3:183 "God bound us by charge (عَهِدَ إِلَيْنَا) that we believe no messenger until..."; 43:49 & 7:134 "by the binding commitment He has with you (بِمَا عَهِدَ عِندَكَ)". In every case the root supplies "a binding obligation established" — the إِلَى frame merely directs it at a recipient.

FORM III (عَاهَدَ, 11 occ.): the derivational reciprocity of Form III supplies mutuality; the root residue is unchanged. 16:91 "when you enter a mutual pact (عَاهَدتُّم)"; 2:100 "whenever they made a covenant (عَاهَدُوا عَهْدًا)"; 33:15 "they had covenanted with God (عَاهَدُوا اللَّهَ) not to turn their backs"; 33:23/48:10 "what they pledged to God upon (عَاهَدُوا اللَّهَ عَلَيْهِ)"; 8:56, 9:1, 9:4, 9:7 "those you made a pact with (عَاهَدتَّ/عَاهَدتُّم)"; 9:75 "covenanted with God that if He gives...". The bond-of-obligation is present throughout; Form III + object (اللَّهَ / مِنْهُم) supplies the counterparties.

NOUN (عَهْد, 29 occ.): names the binding commitment as an object/instrument. The obligation-residue shows in the collocations that presuppose it: fulfilling it — يُوفُونَ بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ (13:20), أَوْفُوا بِعَهْدِي (2:40), الْمُوفُونَ بِعَهْدِهِمْ (2:177); breaking it — يَنقُضُونَ عَهْدَ اللَّهِ (13:25, 2:27), نَبَذَهُ (2:100); trading it away — تَشْتَرُوا/يَشْتَرُونَ بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ (16:95, 3:77); being answerable for it — إِنَّ الْعَهْدَ كَانَ مَسْـُٔولًا (17:34), عَهْدُ اللَّهِ مَسْـُٔولًا (33:15); contracting it — اتَّخَذَ عِندَ الرَّحْمَٰنِ/اللَّهِ عَهْدًا (19:78, 19:87, 2:80); its grant — لَا يَنَالُ عَهْدِي الظَّالِمِينَ (2:124); its absence as unreliability — مَا وَجَدْنَا لِأَكْثَرِهِم مِّنْ عَهْدٍ (7:102); paired with entrusted things — لِأَمَٰنَٰتِهِمْ وَعَهْدِهِمْ رَاعُونَ (23:8, 70:32). In each, "binding obligation to be kept" is exactly what can be fulfilled, broken, sold, or asked about.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: Subtractions performed: (a) FORM — Form I supplies unilateral imposition (a charge laid down), Form III supplies reciprocity (a mutual pact), the maSdar/noun عَهْد supplies reification of the bond as an object; all three retain the invariant "binding obligation." (b) CONSTRUCTION — إِلَى + recipient directs the charge toward someone (Form I); عَلَى marks the matter pledged-upon (33:23, 48:10); بِ marks the commitment as the thing fulfilled/traded (يُوفُونَ بِ, تَشْتَرُوا بِ); عِندَ + party marks the covenant as lodged/held with a counterparty (19:78, 9:7); direct object اللَّهَ / مِنْهُم supplies counterparties. None of these vectors is the root; they position the bond. (c) PARTICIPANTS — God-as-binder (Adam, Abraham, Children of Israel), human-to-God pledges (33:15, 9:75), human-to-human treaties (8:56, 9:1/4/7) — the binder/bound identity is contextual, not root-contributed. (d) CONTEXT — legal/treaty (Surah 9), covenantal-salvific (2:40, 2:124), eschatological accountability (2:80, 19:78, 17:34), narrative (20:115, 2:125) — all peripheral. Residue after subtraction: the bond-of-obligation itself.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 20:86:16:2 — أَفَطَالَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْعَهْدُ ("did the الْعَهْد seem long/protracted to you?"). Here عَهْد is read by some as an elapsed time-span rather than a pledge, which would threaten the "binding obligation" invariant by substituting a purely temporal sense. It reconciles internally: the immediately preceding clause is أَلَمْ يَعِدْكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ وَعْدًا حَسَنًا ("did your Lord not make you a good promise?"), so الْعَهْد resumes precisely the binding engagement/pledge just named — the sense is "did the [term of the] covenant weigh long upon you," i.e. the obligation and its standing period, not bare chronology. The binding-commitment residue is recoverable, with "duration" supplied contextually by طَالَ, not by the root. A second hard case, بِمَا عَهِدَ عِندَكَ (43:49, 7:134), risks reading as bare "what he knows/has with you," but عِندَ + the pleading "invoke your Lord by..." frames it as the standing commitment God holds with the prophet — obligation-residue intact.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: The strongest alternative is that the core is unilateral "charge/injunction — to enjoin a directive" (privileging Form I: God enjoins Adam/Abraham/Children of Adam), with "mutual covenant" treated as a Form III extension. Internal evidence arbitrates against making EITHER pole the root: Form I is transparently unilateral (عَهِدَ إِلَى + أَنْ-clause command) while Form III is transparently reciprocal (عَاهَدَ + counterparty), and the noun spans both (God's imposed عهد in 2:124 vs. negotiated treaties in 9:1/4/7). The only sense common to both poles — and to the noun — is the neutral, directionless "binding obligation established," with directionality (imposed vs. mutual) donated by the FORM. A weaker competitor, "knowledge/acquaintance" (classical عهد = to know), finds no internal foothold: no occurrence turns on cognition rather than obligation. So the abstract obligation-bond, not "charge" and not "acquaintance," is the arbitrated center.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Nearest neighbors, several co-occurring in the same verses: (1) w-ʿ-d وعد "promise" — appears beside this root in 20:86 (يَعِدْكُمْ وَعْدًا vs. الْعَهْد) and 9:111 (وَعْدًا... vs. أَوْفَىٰ بِعَهْدِهِ). وعد announces a future act/outcome one will perform (one-directional forecast); عهد is the binding bond that obligates and is liable to being kept or broken (نقض/نكث/نبذ) and to being asked about (مسؤولًا) — a liability-bearing engagement, not a forecast. (2) w-th-q وثق / مِيثَاق — co-occurs in 13:20, 13:25, 2:27 (عهد ... مِيثَاق). مِيثَاق foregrounds the tightening/ratification of a bond (from "to bind fast"); عهد names the undertaking/commitment as such — note 13:25 "break the عهد of God after its مِيثَاق (its ratification)," where the two are distinguished, عهد = the engagement, مِيثَاق = its solemn confirmation. (3) ʾ-m-n أَمَانَة — paired in 23:8, 70:32 (لِأَمَٰنَٰتِهِمْ وَعَهْدِهِمْ). أمانة = a thing entrusted into one's keeping; عهد = the pledge/commitment one has bound oneself to. FALSIFIABILITY: the invariant fails if any occurrence shows the root meaning a mere future promise with no keep/break-liability dimension and no charge (collapsing it into وعد), or a pure ratification-act (مِيثَاق), or bare acquaintance/time-span with no obligation. No such occurrence exists in these 46.
internal_discovery.rationale: A single non-empty contribution — "a binding obligation/undertaking that stands to be fulfilled or breached" — is surface-recoverable in every one of the 46 occurrences after subtracting form (unilateral Form I charge / reciprocal Form III pact / reified noun), construction (إِلَى, عَلَى, بِ, عِندَ, direct object), participants, and context. The direction is determinate: the root establishes/denotes the bond of obligation, with imposed-vs-mutual polarity donated by the form rather than by the root, so the two poles are a clean layer-split, not an underdetermined center. The keep/break/sell/answer-for collocations (يوفون بـ, ينقضون, نبذ, يشترون بـ, مسؤولًا) presuppose exactly this residue, and the hardest cases (20:86 "protracted covenant"; 43:49/7:134 "the commitment He holds with you") reconcile by anaphora and framing without forcing. The root is sharply distinct from co-occurring وعد (forecast), مِيثَاق (ratification), and أَمَانَة (entrusted thing), each of which the text sets alongside it in contrast. No occurrence resists the invariant; hence PREFERRED at STRONG strength.

adversarial_verification.notes:
Refutation sweep across all 46 occurrences. The candidate ('binding obligation/undertaking') is genuinely robust for 45/46: the noun cluster is defined by predicates that presuppose a standing bond — fulfilling (يوفون/أوفوا: 13:20, 2:40, 2:177, 3:76, 6:152, 9:111, 16:91, 17:34), breaking (ينقضون/نبذ/نكثوا: 2:27, 13:25, 8:56, 2:100, 9:12), trading (تشتروا/يشترون: 16:95, 3:77), being answered for (مسؤولًا: 17:34, 33:15), contracting (اتخذ عند: 2:80, 19:78, 19:87), granting (لا ينال عهدي: 2:124), and its absence as unreliability (7:102). Form III uniformly yields mutual pact/pledge (9:1/9:4/9:7/8:56/9:75/33:15/33:23/48:10/16:91/2:100/2:177); Form I with إلى yields a laid-on binding charge (20:115, 2:125, 36:60, 3:183) or God's standing commitment (43:49, 7:134). None of these falsify.

Hardest case and only genuine failure: 20:86 (word_ref 20:86:16:2), أَفَطَالَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْعَهْدُ. Here ٱلْعَهْد is the subject of طَالَ (grew LONG). Temporal length is predicable of a DURATION/era, not of an obligation-bond; this is the attested lexical sense عهد = 'lapse of time / period' (cf. حديث/قريب العهد), and standard tafsir glosses it as the المدّة of Moses' absence. The same verse contrasts عهد with a distinct وَعْد (وعدًا حسنًا) and مَوْعِد (مَوْعِدي). Reading it as 'did the binding obligation seem long?' smuggles in exactly the temporal residue the frozen candidate expressly disowns — circular/ad-hoc rescue. This is a real polysemy the contribution cannot bridge.

Distinctiveness: OK. The Quranic text itself co-deploys عهد against ميثاق (13:20 ولا ينقضون الميثاق; 2:27/13:25 من بعد ميثاقه) and against وعد, so the candidate cleanly discriminates from nearest neighbors: ميثاق (ratified/tightened compact), وعد (the promised future act), أمانة (entrusted thing, paired but distinguished in 23:8/70:32), عقد (contract). Not a vague blob.

Falsifiability: OK. Clear failure condition exists (a temporal-duration or bare-futurity reading), and 20:86 actually meets it — the contribution is falsifiable and is partially falsified. Verdict PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED rather than REFUTED because the split is a single contested/metonymic temporal occurrence, not a systematic homonymy; 45/46 hold solidly.
